rated-small-inductive-breaking-current: In [[iec-56]] this is clause 4.112, Rated small inductive breaking current, which the 1987 standard records only as "Under consideration" — no standard values are assigned. Conceptually it is the maximum small inductive current (e.g. the magnetizing current of unloaded transformers and reactors, or shunt-reactor current) that the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking at its rated voltage under the prescribed conditions. The defining hazard is current chopping: interrupting a small, lagging inductive current before its natural zero traps magnetic energy that converts to a switching overvoltage on the load side. Because no rated values are tabulated, the duty is demonstrated by the [[magnetizing-and-small-inductive-current-switching-test]] (clause 6.112). It is one of the optional rated quantities listed in the nameplate clause, distinct from capacitive switching ([[rated-line-charging-breaking-current]], [[rated-single-capacitor-bank-breaking-current]]) and from [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]] ([[iec-56]] 4.112).
rated-out-of-phase-breaking-current: Clause 4.106 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated out-of-phase breaking current as the maximum out-of-phase current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking, under the prescribed conditions, in a circuit having the recovery voltage specified below. Out-of-phase conditions (3.101.14) are abnormal states of lost or lacking synchronism between the system parts on either side of the breaker, where the phase angle between the generated-voltage vectors exceeds normal and may reach 180 degrees (phase opposition), so the [[recovery-voltage]] is much higher than for a normal fault. Its specification is not mandatory; if assigned: (a) power-frequency recovery voltage is 2.0/sqrt(3) x rated voltage (earthed-neutral) or 2.5/sqrt(3) (other systems); (b) TRV follows Tables VIA-VID; (c) the current is 25% of the [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]] unless otherwise specified. Verified by the [[out-of-phase-test]] (6.110). See also [[making-and-breaking-capacity]] ([[iec-56]] 4.106).
rated-single-capacitor-bank-breaking-cur: Clause 4.107 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated single capacitor bank breaking current as the maximum capacitor current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking at its rated voltage under the prescribed conditions of use and behaviour, without exceeding the maximum permissible switching overvoltages specified by the manufacturer (suggested values in Table IX, columns B). It refers explicitly to switching a shunt capacitor bank where no shunt capacitors are connected to the source side of the breaker — a single capacitor bank (3.101.11) whose inrush is limited only by supply inductance and the bank's own capacitance. This contrasts with the [[rated-back-to-back-capacitor-bank-breaking-current]], where parallel banks raise the inrush. Specification is not mandatory; values are selected from the R 10 series. The principal hazard on interruption is [[restrike]] producing voltage escalation; verified by the [[capacitive-current-switching-test]] ([[iec-56]] 4.107).
rated-line-charging-breaking-current: Clause 4.107 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated line-charging breaking current as the maximum line-charging (capacitive) current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking at its rated voltage under the prescribed conditions of use and behaviour, without exceeding the maximum permissible switching overvoltages specified by the manufacturer (suggested values in Table IX). This is the duty of switching off an unloaded overhead line, where the breaker interrupts the line's distributed charging current and a one-cosine [[recovery-voltage]] builds across the gap as the trapped charge holds the line side near peak voltage. Its specification is confined to three-pole breakers for switching three-phase overhead lines with rated voltage at or above 72.5 kV; standard values appear in Table VII (e.g. 10 A at 72.5 kV up to 500 A at 525 kV). A Table VII note ties the values to roughly 1.2 x U km of single-conductor line at 50 Hz. The chief concern is [[restrike]]; verified by the [[capacitive-current-switching-test]] ([[iec-56]] 4.107).
rated-cable-charging-breaking-current: Clause 4.108 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated cable-charging breaking current as the maximum cable-charging (capacitive) current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking at its rated voltage under the prescribed conditions of use and behaviour, without exceeding the appropriate maximum permissible switching overvoltages specified by the manufacturer (suggested values in Table IX). It represents switching off an unloaded insulated cable operating at no load, the analogue for cables of the [[rated-line-charging-breaking-current]]. Specifying it is not mandatory but is made on request, and is considered unnecessary for breakers of rated voltage at or below 24 kV; if assigned, values should follow Table VIII (e.g. 10 A at 3.6 kV rising to 500 A at 525 kV). A Table VIII note states these cover the normal maximum needs of most power systems, with higher currents subject to special agreement. Because cable capacitance is large, [[restrike]] and the resulting [[recovery-voltage]] escalation dominate; verified by the [[capacitive-current-switching-test]] ([[iec-56]] 4.108).
rated-back-to-back-capacitor-bank-breaki: Clause 4.110 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated back-to-back capacitor bank breaking current as the maximum capacitor current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of breaking at its rated voltage under the prescribed conditions, without exceeding the maximum permissible switching overvoltages specified by the manufacturer (suggested values in Table IX, columns B). It refers to switching a shunt capacitor bank where one or several other shunt banks are connected to the source side, so the breaker sees a multiple (parallel) / back-to-back bank (3.101.12): on closing, the already-energised parallel banks discharge into the bank being switched, giving a high-frequency inrush equal to the [[rated-capacitor-bank-inrush-making-current]]. This distinguishes it from the [[rated-single-capacitor-bank-breaking-current]], where no source-side banks exist. Specification is not mandatory; values come from the R 10 series, and a note adds that similar conditions can apply to switching cables. [[restrike]] on interruption is the key risk; see [[capacitive-current-switching-test]] ([[iec-56]] 4.110).
rated-capacitor-bank-inrush-making-curre: Clause 4.111 of [[iec-56]] defines the rated capacitor bank inrush making current as the peak value of current the circuit-breaker shall be capable of making at its rated voltage, with a frequency of the inrush current appropriate to the service conditions (see Appendix BB). Unlike the breaking quantities, this is a making duty: when a capacitor bank is energised — especially in a back-to-back arrangement — the parallel banks discharge into the bank being switched, producing a brief high-amplitude, high-frequency current surge that stresses the closing contacts and pre-arc. Specifying it is mandatory for any breaker assigned a [[rated-back-to-back-capacitor-bank-breaking-current]]. Values are selected from the R 10 series. Notes state the service inrush frequency is normally 2-5 kHz, and that a breaker tested at one frequency is deemed suitable for any lower inrush frequency. It is the making counterpart to the capacitive breaking duties; see [[making-and-breaking-capacity]] and [[capacitive-current-switching-test]] ([[iec-56]] 4.111).
making-and-breaking-capacity: In [[iec-56]] these capacities are the characteristic quantities defined in sub-clause 3.105. Breaking capacity (3.105.12, IEV 441-17-08) is a value of current a circuit-breaker can break under prescribed conditions of use and behaviour; making capacity (3.105.16, 441-17-09) is the corresponding quantity for making. The standard specialises breaking capacity by duty: line-charging (3.105.13), cable-charging (3.105.14) and capacitor bank (3.105.15) breaking capacities each name the specified opening of an unloaded line, cable or capacitor bank, while short-circuit making/breaking capacities are 3.105.18/3.105.19. Out-of-phase (making or breaking) capacity (3.105.17) covers operation during loss or lack of synchronism on either side of the breaker. A note records that earlier editions used "rated making capacity"/"rated breaking capacity"; current usage conveys this through the rated currents themselves — e.g. [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]], [[rated-out-of-phase-breaking-current]] and [[rated-capacitor-bank-inrush-making-current]] ([[iec-56]] 3.105).
